Olga / Marissa — attaching the redacted summary and a short vuln-management overview. Key points for HealthSync: 

- Penetration testing cadence: full external penetration test annually, internal security scans quarterly, and scheduled dependency scanning monthly (Snyk/OSS). We also run targeted re-tests after major releases or config changes.
- Recent tests: last external third-party test: May 2027 (summary attached). We do not share raw exploit PoCs; we provide findings with risk ratings and remediation guidance.
- Vulnerability SLA: critical (P0) — acknowledge within 24 hours, mitigation plan within 72 hours, patch/mitigation in 30 days where feasible; high (P1) — acknowledge 72 hours, remediation goal 90 days; medium/low — managed in regular sprints (180 days for medium typically). For HIPAA-sensitive paths we accelerate timelines in coordination with customers.
- Disclosure policy: coordinated disclosure — we maintain a security@redwood.com mailbox. We will notify affected customers within the SLA windows above and provide a public advisory only when coordinated and redaction-safe. We support responsible disclosure and have a bug bounty / triage flow for externally reported issues (details in playbook).

Attachments included: redwood-pentest-summary-stub.pdf (redacted), vuln-management-playbook-summary.txt (operational summary).

If HealthSync wants a tailored remediation SLA or a mutually-agreed handback window for a white-glove deployment, we can draft that into the mutual action plan.

— Diego Fernandez
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
